artworks.title: Oedipus Separating from Jocasta
artworks.description: Cabanel's early academic canvas freezes the palace catastrophe: Oedipus turns from Jocasta as recognition unmakes their marriage. The queen who was mother and wife stands at the hinge of Sophocles' plot — the moment before the noose.

artworks.title: Farewell of Oedipus to the Corpses of His Wife and Sons
artworks.description: Toudouze's Prix de Rome painting (École des Beaux-Arts, Paris) lays Jocasta among the dead of the house of Cadmus. Blind Oedipus takes leave of the queen who hanged herself when the bed's riddle was spoken — Theban ruin staged as a funeral farewell.

artworks.title: Oedipus and Jocasta
artworks.description: Bernard's late modernist pair keeps mother and son in the same charged space — Jocasta as consort before the recognition, the double bond made visible without the Sphinx or the noose. A twentieth-century return to the Theban queen at the heart of the tragedy.

artworks.title: Eteocles and Polynices Admonished to Peace by Their Mother Jocasta
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print (CC0): Jocasta stands between her warring sons, pleading for peace before the Seven march on Thebes. The queen as mediator — the mother who cannot stop the brothers' mutual slaughter that will leave Creon the throne.

artworks.title: Jocasta and Oedipus
artworks.description: Hand-colored German woodcut from Steinhöwel's Boccaccio: Jocasta and her son Oedipus as a famous woman of antiquity. Early print culture already fixed the Theban queen beside the son who was also her husband.

films.title: Edipo re
films.description: Pasolini's Jocasta is mother and wife in the same frame — the queen who hangs herself when the riddle of the bed is finally spoken aloud.

films.title: Oedipus the King
films.description: Saville's adaptation keeps Jocasta in the palace recognition — the mother who sees the truth a breath before her son does.

music.title: Oedipus Rex
music.description: In Stravinsky's Latin ritual Jocasta's voice cuts the oratorio's stone — the queen whose aria knows too much before the messenger arrives.

popCulture.title: Oedipus Rex
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' queen who hung herself when the bed's riddle was spoken — mother and wife in the same recognition, the palace's silent collapse.
